title: Persona card
description: A persona lives in personas/*.yaml, versioned independently of agent code so it can be reviewed and diffed like any other artifact. DESIGN.md section 4.

summary.description: Who this is, in a few sentences. This is the text re-injected by persona-drift-check, so it must stand alone without the rest of the card.

goals.description: What this person is trying to accomplish, in their terms.

success_criteria.description: The completion test for the session. DESIGN.md section 3: these are the stopping condition, so they must be observable from the outside, not 'the user feels satisfied'.

out_of_scope.description: Surfaces this persona would never touch. Prevents drift into areas where any finding would be an artifact of the agent, not the persona.

reading.description: The single highest-signal behavioural dial. Most drift shows up here first: a 'skims' persona that starts reading error messages closely has already drifted.

retry_tolerance.description: How many times this person retries a failing action before giving up. A methodical QA engineer retries indefinitely; almost no real persona does.

uses.description: Words this person actually reaches for. Advisory only -- not mechanically checked.

never_uses.description:
Terms this person does not have. Two characters is the floor because most Chinese and Japanese technical terms are two characters long (模型, 後端). Matched case-insensitively against the session log by `pqa drift`, which is a deterministic string check rather than a model call -- a cheap tripwire for a failure that would otherwise need another agent to notice.

A minimum of 5 is required: an empty or near-empty list silently disables the tripwire, and a disabled check that still appears to run is worse than no check.

tells.description: Concrete in-character behaviours the evaluator can look for, e.g. 'closes modals without reading them'.
